newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA MAY CONSUMER PRICE INDEX UP 9.5 PCT Y/Y.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MAY CONSUMER PRICE INDEX UP 9.5 PCT Y/Y.

text.p: South Africa's all-items consumer price index rose 0.3 percent in May from April after rising 0.9 percent in April, the Central Statistical Service said.
The year-on-year rise was 9.5 percent versus April's 9.9 percent.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast a 0.6 percent month-on-month increase and a 9.8 percent year-on-year rise.
The CSS said food inflation reached was at the highest level
since October 1996, at an annual rate of 11.7 percent.
The Central Statistical Service's survey of consumer prices
is now broken down into five expenditure groups. The old system
of breaking the survey down into three income groups has fallen
away and as a result, those indices are no longer applicable.
Month-on-month percentage changes in the expenditure groups are
thus only available from February 1997, while year-on-year
percentage changes will only be calculated from January 1998.
NOTE - The December and January 1996 all items and food
indices have been revised to take account of the change in the
base year to 1995 from 1990 which took effect in January this
CSS has also introduced a core inflation rate which excludes
value added tax; fresh and frozen meat and fish, fresh and
frozen vegetables and fresh fruit and nuts; interest rates on
mortgage bonds and overdrafts/personal loans; and property
As this is a new index, month-on-month percentage changes
have been be calculated from February 1997 and a year-on-year
percentage change will be calculated from January 1998.
